notes: Which engine model Imajutsu uses for each mode, in order of preference. This file is DATA: reorder the lists, edit the reasons, add a model. Code never names a model. The first model in a list that is installed, allowed for the person, and really offers the engine mode (the engine registry's capabilities.modes) is the recommended one. Facts measured on the DGX Spark (docs/imajutsu-bench/), corrected run at each model's OWN default steps and guidance (720x1280, 9:16, 7 scene types). 'quality' lists the draft and high step counts; the standard count is always the engine's own default for the model. 'wording' says how the prompt builder writes for a model: 'natural' = natural sentences ('handheld phone photo' is fine), 'plain' = 'A photograph of ...' plus plain light and framing sentences and none of the model's avoid_words.

flux2-klein-4b.seconds_hint: about 4 s for 720x1280 at its own 4 steps (guidance 1.0)

z-image-turbo.seconds_hint: about 12 s for 720x1280 at its own 9 steps (guidance 0)

qwen-image-2512.seconds_hint: about 86 s for 720x1280 at 30 steps (iPhone Photo); 145 s at its own 50 steps
qwen-image-2512.preset_steps_evidence: 2026-11-07, 720x1280, 4 scenes, same seed: 30 steps is visually the same as the engine default 50 (86 s vs 145 s); 20 steps (58 s) shows softer faces and motion smear in low light, so 20 stays the draft count.

models.why: The most convincing casual phone-style generator in the benchmark, including selfies, mirror shots and night scenes (natural light, believable geometry), and fast: about 4 s for a 720x1280 picture at its own 4 steps and guidance 1.0.
evidence: docs/imajutsu-bench/ (re-run at default steps 4 / guidance 1.0): FLUX.2 klein 4B ranked first for casual photographic prompts

models.why: Polished, slightly glamorous pictures and very good vehicle geometry with plain descriptive prompts; about 12 s for 720x1280 at its own 9 steps and guidance 0.
evidence: docs/imajutsu-bench/ (re-run at default steps): still draws a hand holding a phone when the prompt says 'phone'; no longer produces poster graphics

models.why: Highest realism of the installed models for plain prompts, but 50 steps take about 2.5 minutes per picture.
evidence: docs/imajutsu-bench/ 2026-11-06: minutes per image on the GB10; results still being judged

models.why: Fast (about 4 s): the most convincing casual phone look in the corrected benchmark, wide-angle, good night and neon scenes, strong prompt adherence. One click away (Fast) for quick iterations; the default tier is Best realism.
evidence: docs/imajutsu-bench/run3 (each model at its own defaults): FLUX.2 klein 4B is the fast option with a convincing phone look

models.why: Best realism (about 1.5 min per picture at 30 steps): real skin, natural expressions, accurate vehicles, believable unflattering mirror selfies and family scenes, when prompted in plain words. Recommended for final photos.
evidence: docs/imajutsu-bench/run3: qwen-image-2512 (50 steps, guidance 4) gave the most convincing casual smartphone-style photos
'snapshot' / 'candid phone' make it draw a selfie in the foreground, so the builder never writes them

models.why: Polished and slightly glamorous (about 12 s), excellent vehicle geometry. It needs plain wording: the prompt must not say 'phone', or it draws a hand holding one.
evidence: docs/imajutsu-bench/run3: z-image-turbo (9 steps, guidance 0) draws a hand holding a phone when the prompt says 'phone'

models.why: A dedicated instruction-editing model: it takes the picture and up to two more, and follows edit sentences closely. Slow (about 40 steps).
evidence: docs/IMAJUTSU.md: qwen-image-edit-2511 edit with up to 3 pictures

models.why: Fast instruction editing (about 20 s) with the picture and up to three more.
evidence: docs/IMAJUTSU.md: flux2-klein-4b edit with up to 4 pictures

models.why: Follows 'replace X with the subject in image 2' instructions with the source and up to two reference pictures.
evidence: docs/IMAJUTSU.md: qwen-image-edit-2511 edit with up to 3 pictures

models.why: Fast; takes the source and up to three reference pictures, and can inpaint inside a selection.
evidence: docs/IMAJUTSU.md: flux2-klein-4b edit with up to 4 pictures and inpaint

models.why: Fast inpainting that can also use reference pictures. Inpaint words are sent as an instruction ('Fill the selected area with ...') because this model draws nothing from a bare noun phrase.
models.inpaint_prompt: Fill the selected area with {text}. Keep the lighting, perspective and style of the rest of the picture.
models.preset_steps_evidence: 2026-11-08, 720x1280, same seed: with a noun phrase ('A potted green plant') FLUX.2 klein drew nothing in the selection; told what to do ('Fill the selected area with a potted green plant ...') it drew the pot, and a larger selection with 8 steps (12 s instead of 6 s) drew a full plant.

models.why: Inpainting with plain descriptive prompts.
Slow, high-detail inpainting.
Fast; the new area is a masked region of a padded canvas.
Plain-prompt outpainting.
Slow, high-detail outpainting.
Takes up to four reference pictures and makes a new picture guided by them.
Takes up to three pictures; slower.
Image-to-image at a chosen strength: keeps the layout and changes the look.
Slow, high-detail image-to-image.
Restyles by instruction instead of strength.
Fast restyling by instruction.

refine.why: An optional second pass at low strength after scaling; it can add texture, so it is a model step and is labelled as one.

models.why: Fast and flexible: text, edit and inpaint.
Text, image-to-image and inpaint with plain prompts.
Text, image-to-image and inpaint, slow.
Instruction editing.
